privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes the data used to operate a NonbiriAPI alpha.3 instance.
privacy.notice: Deployment template: before accepting real users, the instance operator must replace the operator identity, contact channel, effective date, retention details and governing-law statements as required by the deployment and applicable law. This text is not legal advice.
privacy.operatorBody: NonbiriAPI is open-source software. Each deployed instance is operated independently by the person or organization that controls that instance. This policy applies to data processed by that operator, not to the public source repository or to Discord and upstream providers acting under their own policies.
privacy.identityBody: The user station uses Discord OAuth for registration and sign-in. The service receives a Discord identifier, username, avatar metadata and the membership information needed for a configured server-and-role registration gate. OAuth access tokens are used during the exchange and are not stored as account data. The service stores bounded account, session and preference metadata. Session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite according to the deployment configuration.
privacy.dataBody: The service stores account-owned endpoint metadata, canonical upstream URLs, notes, enabled flags, connector types, fetched model identifiers, platform model names, routing choices and bindings. An OpenAI-compatible physical key may store the force_store_false policy, and a personal OpenAI-compatible logical model may store the flatten_tool_calls policy; these are booleans, not request content. Upstream credentials are encrypted at rest. A caller key is shown once and only irreversible lookup material and display fragments remain. The service also stores check-in, donation/charity, daily activity, ban, limit, game-profile visibility, server-generated game settlement/outcome/best, and bounded anti-abuse/accounting metadata. Export schema version 4 adds safe endpoint origin and donated-key authorized/effective expiry and safe source fields. It includes only allowlisted account metadata and excludes secrets, ciphertext, report fingerprints, source key identities, administrator notes, OAuth tokens, caller-key plaintext, Debug content, random entropy and other users' identities.
privacy.economyBody: The service stores your single spendable Nonbiri credit balance, which may be negative, together with check-in awards, game payouts and charity-routing summaries. Check-in awards, donor rewards and game payouts add to the same spendable balance; charity routing and game entry costs debit it. donation_credit is a cumulative donor-reward statistic used for donor summaries and level thresholds; it is not a second wallet. Ordinary spending, check-ins and natural game events do not change that statistic. Every balance change has an append-only ledger row. Fishing prices, cryptographic random outcomes, reserves, recovery and settlement are server-authoritative; no catch or economic return is guaranteed, and level 4 provides no game-economy advantage. Leaderboard rows are anonymous by default; an explicit public preference publishes the current nickname/username and a static 64px Discord CDN avatar URL together. The service does not proxy/cache that avatar or copy profile identity into historical game rows.
privacy.credentialsBody: Upstream secrets are never returned in ordinary lists, logs, alerts, errors, exports or URLs. The browser receives key metadata only and does not persist upstream secrets or caller-key plaintext in storage or the query cache. Key or account deletion revokes callable authority in the final transaction, and orphaned encrypted credential material is cleared within at most one hour. An OpenAI-compatible key may force the outbound store field to false, but an upstream may ignore or reject it; this is not a zero-retention guarantee and does not control provider abuse monitoring. Operators must still protect the server, complete snapshots and master-key file.
privacy.trafficBody: Forwarded requests produce bounded metadata such as account, model, upstream endpoint, timestamps, status, duration and available token usage; ordinary request and response content is not persisted. Debug always starts as a dry run that does not select a candidate, access a credential, perform DNS/egress, reserve charity credits, or write usage/activity. Actual send is a separate switch requiring a fresh in-site confirmation and may incur provider usage or charity accounting. Redacted, bounded request/response projections exist only in process and current-page memory and are never written to the database, ordinary logs, alerts, exports, backups, URLs or browser storage; session close, replacement, expiry, logout, ban, deletion or restart clears them. A Debug page/SSE disconnect does not cancel the original CallerKey request. Administrators and live level-5 stewards see bounded metadata only, with donated resources hidden from the steward projection.
privacy.sharingBody: Request content may be sent to OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible endpoints selected by the account owner, including donor-provided charity resources operated by OpenAI, Anthropic or another independent third party. The provider may process or retain content, account logs or abuse-monitoring data under its own policy; the instance operator cannot control third-party retention. A charity donor, as controller of the corresponding upstream account or key, may be able to see the full request content in the provider's backend logs; the instance UI itself does not disclose the consumer's identity or request body to the donor. Each forwarded request also carries a server-generated safety pseudonym that is linkable only within the same user, deployment key and canonical upstream origin, so it is pseudonymous rather than anonymous. Discord processes OAuth activity under Discord's policy. The operator may disclose data as required by law or to protect the service, users or public safety and must document other processors, hosting and support access.
privacy.retentionBody: Request logs are cleaned after up to 30 days; terminal donation/review facts, daily activity summaries and terminal charity reservations after 400 days. An irreversible fingerprint used only to match newly submitted abuse reports may remain for up to 90 days after a donated key ends or its physical key is deleted; it cannot authorize an upstream call. Minimal target and donation-lineage facts already established for a report case follow that case's own 90-day or active legal-hold lifecycle. Reads do not refresh these deadlines, and legal hold does not extend the fingerprint matching window. Terminal game round, settlement and outcome rows are cleaned 30 days after settlement, while a paid pending round is retained until settlement. Game best, game ledger and profile-visibility preference remain for the account lifetime. Debug content has no persistent retention. Sessions expire by idle and absolute TTL. Resolved administrator alerts are cleaned 30 days after resolution; pending alerts are bounded by total and per-kind caps plus deduplication. Export schema version 4 caps every collection at 10,000 rows and the complete JSON at 8 MiB and fails closed instead of truncating. Account deletion invalidates sessions and CallerKeys, clears private linked data, and leaves only lifecycle-governed deidentified facts; late callbacks cannot recreate the account. Complete operator snapshots and upstream providers may retain copies under their respective policies.
privacy.rightsBody: Subject to applicable law and the instance operator's process, you can update supported account settings, request an export and delete your account through the elevated self-service flow. Deletion is destructive. Contact the instance operator for access, correction, restriction or other privacy requests; the operator must publish the appropriate contact channel before production use.
privacy.securityBody: The service applies ownership checks, encrypted secret storage, outbound SSRF and redirect protections, bounded resources, cancellation propagation and no-store responses to sensitive APIs. The OpenAI-only flatten_tool_calls experiment changes structured calls into text, restores only complete real call/result pairs, never executes tools or fabricates results, and may break normal tool workflows; Anthropic bindings are incompatible with it. No system is completely secure. Do not place secrets in notes, model names, URLs, tool data, issue reports or support messages.
privacy.contactBody: The instance operator must publish a privacy contact, effective date and applicable jurisdiction in this page before production use. Material changes to data collection, sharing or retention should be announced and handled according to applicable law.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: By using a NonbiriAPI instance, you agree to use it lawfully and protect your own credentials.
terms.notice: Deployment template: the instance operator must replace the operator identity, contact channel, effective date, governing law and complaint process before accepting real users. This text is not legal advice.
terms.operatorBody: NonbiriAPI is open-source gateway software, not an AI model provider. The operator of the particular instance controls its access policy, configured upstreams, limits, maintenance and user support. The public source project and its copyright holder do not automatically operate every deployment.
terms.accessBody: An account may require Discord OAuth and membership of a configured server and role. You are responsible for activity performed through your account and must provide information that is accurate enough for the operator's access and support process. The operator may pause new registration or suspend access for security, maintenance, legal compliance or a breach of these terms.
terms.useBody: Use only endpoints, credentials and models that you are authorized to access. Do not use the service for unlawful activity, fraud, abuse, unauthorized access, credential theft, malware, harassment, privacy violations, sexual exploitation of minors, non-consensual intimate imagery, attacks against providers or other users, denial of service, rate-limit bypassing or attempts to defeat ownership and security controls.
terms.upstreamBody: Requests may be processed by account-selected OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible providers, including a donor-provided charity resource. You must comply with each provider's terms, usage policies, licensing conditions and content restrictions. Providers may retain request content, account logs or abuse-monitoring data under their own policies. A requested store:false field may be ignored or rejected and is not a promise of zero retention. The operator does not guarantee provider acceptance, content preservation or account availability.
terms.credentialsBody: Keep upstream credentials, caller keys, OAuth links and recovery information confidential. Rotate a credential immediately if it may have been exposed. Do not put secrets in notes, URLs, model names, tools, issue reports or support messages. You are responsible for submitted content and the rights needed to send it to the selected provider. Experimental tool-call flattening only changes representation: it does not execute a tool, create a result or prove success, and it may break an ordinary structured-tool client.
terms.availabilityBody: Requests may be limited, rejected, retried or unavailable because of quotas, ownership checks, safety controls, upstream failures, maintenance or authorization. A complete protocol response, not HTTP status alone, determines success. Debug dry-run sends nothing upstream; a separately confirmed live mode may consume provider quota or charity credits. Game prices, random outcomes, recovery and settlement are server-controlled and offer no guaranteed result or return. The operator may change limits or discontinue an alpha service.
terms.dataBody: The privacy policy describes metadata, Debug handling, export and deletion controls. Account deletion is destructive and removes linked donation, charity, check-in, ledger and game data after elevated confirmation. Alpha.3 uses a fresh-only database generation: old, unknown or corrupt databases are rejected before startup writes. A separately confirmed destructive fresh deployment deletes the active database, including accounts, business data, site configuration and legal overrides, and does not merge old data; a protected operator snapshot may retain the previous database, release, environment and master key for rollback. The fresh target must remain in maintenance with registration closed until approved legal text, required configuration and initialization have been reapplied and read back. Snapshot restore/inventory actions and upstream retention follow their own operator/provider policies.
terms.suspensionBody: The operator may suspend or terminate access when reasonably necessary to protect the service or users, comply with law or investigate a suspected breach. Where safe and lawful, the operator may provide notice. You may stop using the service and request account deletion through the supported flow.
terms.liabilityBody: To the extent permitted by applicable law, the service is provided on an as-is and as-available basis without a promise of uninterrupted operation, error-free routing, model accuracy, data availability or fitness for a particular purpose. The operator is not responsible for upstream provider decisions or content generated by upstream systems. Nothing in these terms excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.
terms.ipBody: The NonbiriAPI source code is available under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0. NonbiriAPI, Discord, OpenAI and other names may be trademarks of their respective owners; this project is not automatically affiliated with or endorsed by upstream providers. Rights in submitted or generated content depend on your rights, applicable law and upstream terms.
terms.changesBody: The operator may update these terms for a new release or operational change. Material changes should state an effective date and be communicated as required by applicable law. Continued use after the effective date constitutes acceptance where legally valid; otherwise stop using the service and contact the operator. The operator must publish a contact channel and governing-law statement before production use.
